119.t: Mentor Dean Earl and choosing a school
119.s: Bandleader Dean Earl teaches him manners, professionalism and sensible habits and steers him away from Berklee toward a teaching degree.
119.q: and he says, “good sound.” And you know, encouragement. And in this little joint, Eddie Levine’s, I met all kinds of musicians, they used to come up and visit our leader, who was Dean Earl. And as far as my style and being a gentleman and being in the business and all that, was a fellow by the name…

494.s: Bill's role at Wesleyan and the story of Kenny Washington at Muse.
494.q: Yeah, he was there. I never saw him in action, teaching. Well, no, that’s not true. At Muse, in Brooklyn, which was a community thing, I got a chance to check him out. Yeah, he was a really great teacher. Kenny Washington told me this story. Kenny was a kid. They had sessions there for young…

16.s: After the Navy he studied the Schillinger system with Rudolph Schramm and explains its mathematical view of rhythm in music.
16.q: Yeah. Well when I came out of the Navy, I found that I had, was entitled to post graduate work to take further schooling and I elected to go to NYU to take a course with Rudolph Schramm in the Schilinger system of music and that's what that was about.

508.t: What Berklee gave him: peer listening more than instruction
508.s: Billy Pierce and others pointed him to records, but he says music is about hearing and learned mostly from friends.
508.q: Pierce told me to listen to Impulse Trane. Ed Tomassi told me I needed to check out some Bird. Orville Wright had a calypso class that was great. A lot of the P rooms…practice…the E rooms, the ensemble rooms, a lot of jam sessions at night with the guys. A lot of records being exchanged. A lot of…

136.t: Arriving in Boston and studying at Berklee
136.s: Greeted by Berk, George Wein and Harry Paul, she studies theory and Schillinger and says theory follows music.
136.ch: Boston, Berklee and New York encounters
136.q: Well, first, as I said before, I landed at two o‟clock in the morning, Sunday morning. And uh, three men, the first time I met: it was George Wein, uh, the founder, Lawrence Berk, then George Wein‟s Newport festival‟s public relations person, called Harry Paul. Those three people came to greet me…

406.t: Getting a high school diploma and studying at Juilliard
406.s: While on the staff he finished high school at Rhodes, studied Schillinger with Tom Timothy and entered Juilliard on a friend's urging. His Juilliard teacher borrowed from his Schillinger knowledge.
406.q: Metropole was running big. So now while I was on the staff I decided to go back to school. And I went to Rhodes School (PHONETIC) and got my high school diploma. And really I did that because I was studying the Schillinger system with Tom Timothy and so one day I walked out and ran into Rodriguez --

113.t: Studying at the Kansas City Conservatory
113.s: With his kids in school he enrolled at the Conservatory to learn harmony, composition, ear training and to read, wanting to know what he was doing.
113.q: Oh, yes. Well, what happened, I knew that my kids were getting up in age, and they was going to have to go to school somewhere, so that's why I decided to go to Kansas City. So I figured while they're in school, then I would go to school. So I went to the Conservatory.

148.t: Back to NYU downtown and composition with Marion Bauer
148.s: After Juilliard he took courses at NYU's downtown school and studied composition with Marion Bauer, again rejecting opinions as teaching.
148.q: nothing, so then I tried Julliard but nothing happened there and then I went back--when I went to N.Y.U. originally for pre-med that was the uptown place; that's become Bronx Community College today.

235.t: Studying at Boston Conservatory, Andy Jacobson and his teaching studio
235.s: He studied theory, harmony and sight singing daily, took lessons from Andy Jacobson, opened a studio over the Savoy, met his wife and earned about 150 dollars a week.
235.q: Oh yeah, that's why I went, 'cause I wanted to study and Sabby told me he had a steady job and I said to myself, "Well, this is a chance to get to some things that I wanted to get to, like theory and harmony and sight singing," and so I got into that. And then I met Andy Jacobson and I took some…

389.t: Schillinger course at NYU with Eubie Blake as a classmate
389.s: He finished the NYU course under the GI bill, with Eubie Blake and Eddie Barefield in his class, and found he lacked the talent for background writing.
389.q: The Schillinger method, given by a guy by the name of Rudy Schrann. And Paul Start, of all people, was one of his cohorts.

124.t: Brothers Dave and Bob; Schillinger method
124.s: After the Club Kentucky closed, McRae played with brother Dave in White Plains; Bob studied at Juilliard, prompting talk of the Schillinger system.
124.ch: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
124.q: : Yeah. I had a brother -- my brother, Dave, lived in Westchester. That's when he got together with a band. He had a band up in

78.t: Studying arranging and theory in New York
78.s: Horace began arranging on his own; the Schillinger system was a fad among Fletcher's men, and he enrolled for theory and harmony with Damrosch but did not stay.
78.ch: Starting out in New York and Chicago
78.q: I had begun to kind of go out on my own, and I began to study a few things, and I went to school a little bit in New York.

239.t: Learning to conduct: NYU courses while with Sarah Vaughan
239.s: He wanted to be a writer and took correspondence courses at NYU while with Sarah, then moved from the piano to the podium.
239.q: Just a thing that I wanted to do. I always felt in my heart that I was going to be a writer. And if you're going to be a writer you have to learn how to conduct your material.
